capabilities.scope: On one operator-reported V1.2 sample, normal POWER boot of the R3 NOR FIT and LittleFS image reached NetBSD 11.1 ESP_MOSAICO_LITTLEFS_NOR #6, mounted the 10 MiB littlefs root from flash1 at 0x600000, and reached the final Startup complete message. A subsequent pinned-host-key SSH session succeeded and stayed connected for 52 seconds; WPA status was COMPLETED with SAE and IPv4 present during the session. The /var/run/rc.log interval was 4 minutes 43 seconds with rc exit status 0; the device clock reported a date in 2010, so only the within-log interval is recorded. A separate normal POWER boot of the R4 network-appliance profile completed rc in 189 seconds. The operator saw the logo and service messages. The station reported SAE with PMF and had IPv4, and pinned SSH connected by mDNS name. Earlier bounded tests on this sample reached a single-user shell, retained a synced marker across one normal power cycle, and passed a read-write remount plus write/sync/read smoke check; a RAM-loaded run passed the full VFS checker against the NOR root. This does not establish repeated-cycle reliability, sudden-power-loss durability, full services, NAND, full PSRAM read/write or general peripheral support.

On one operator-reported V1.2 sample, a littlefs root on NOR flash1 (10 MiB at 0x600000) was mounted and operated after a RAM-loaded boot. The read-write remount, full VFS checker and sync passed. A separate ordinary NOR boot reached a single-user shell, retained an earlier synced marker across one normal POWER off/on, and passed a read-write remount plus bounded write/sync/read smoke check. This does not establish crash or sudden-power-loss durability, repeated-cycle reliability, NAND filesystems or sustained operation.

On one operator-reported V1.2 sample, ordinary NOR boot with ESP_MOSAICO_LITTLEFS_NOR kernel #31 and a 10 MiB LittleFS root was followed by one bounded strict-SAE probe. The connected scan preserved the association; ROAM reached the requested alternate BSSID, which matched the final BSSID and differed from baseline. Post-roam status was WPA_COMPLETED/SAE/PMF=1; IPv4 was confirmed with ifconfig, and DNS plus gateway ping passed. A separate later pinned-host-key SSH session after R3 startup remained connected for 52 seconds with WPA COMPLETED/SAE and IPv4 present. These are bounded scenarios, not sustained network acceptance. Host getaddrinfo resolved the assigned .local name to the target interface IPv4. A separate temporary WPA2-PSK profile reached WPA2-PSK/COMPLETED and host ping passed. A later router-side association view showed WPA3-PSK/PMF restored on the original AP. The shared station Action path is now integrated. A RAM probe with EmberBSD 44b8639 preserved SAE/PMF and SSH and reported correlated BTM TX completion; the firmware callback leaves peer ACK unconfirmed. The installed supplicant rejected Neighbor Report locally because its RRM connection state was unset. No RRM/BTM peer exchange was established. AP-initiated BTM/802.11v and 802.11r, forged-frame protection, throughput and sustained reliability remain unverified.

Type-C USB-OTG ROM connection and complete 16 MiB NOR readback were verified with esptool 5.6.0. The board kernel has no S31 USB OTG role/controller integration. Dedicated package pads 44/45 are USB_D+/USB_D−, separate from GPIO44 LCD reset and GPIO45 audio PA enable. Host VBUS/CC role and power behavior are not verified; this does not establish EmberBSD USB support.

On one V1.2 sample, the standard CO5300 framebuffer/genfb/LVGL path displayed a visible interface after the published two-row RASET fix; the user also confirmed changing touch coordinates. This is one RAM-only scenario, not acceptance of other revisions. A later normal POWER boot with the R3 root displayed the fixed MOSAICO, 21 C and SUNNY LVGL sample on a dark background. The EmberBSD QML weather example rendered 21 C and -8 C in one process. After R4 boot the operator confirmed -8 C on the physical display. The same executable had individual RSS samples of 468 KiB and 908 KiB across the two runs. The weather samples do not read sensors or online weather. Touch orientation, quantitative calibration and sustained operation remain unverified. Factory camera preview is vendor-firmware evidence; the R5 video(4) device reported 640 × 480 UYVY. EmberBSD frame delivery remains unverified. The mode table requires 20 MHz XCLK and names 15 fps; fitted oscillator frequency and actual frame rate are unmeasured. EmberBSD radio evidence includes bounded WPA2/SAE handshakes and small/1400-byte gateway ICMP reachability on one sample; one bounded roam succeeded; repeated roaming and sustained operation remain unverified.

On NOR kernel #11, envsys reported valid readings for all six BMI270 accelerometer/gyroscope axes and all four BQ27220 gauge channels. The first BMM150 returned three valid axes; the second returned valid X and Z with invalid Y. The test sampled one board without a motion or calibration reference.

The operator heard the onboard speaker on RAM kernels #18 and #19. On RAM kernel #19 the ES8311 delivered 48000 mono PCM16 samples in 0.993 s. During a two-clap test, two above-background transients were measured 1.005 s apart.

The board tree enables SPI3 and the published source adds a read-only NAND ID/status utility with a staged RV32 binary. It has not been run on hardware or installed in a root image; NAND data reads, ECC, bad-block management, filesystems and boot are not established.

On one V1.2 sample the left-slot module had a CRC-valid EEPROM descriptor (hardware-version field 0x0102). The factory firmware identified SC101IOT PID 0xda4a and displayed a changing 1280 × 720 UYVY preview. EmberBSD identified the same sensor at SCCB address 0x68 and delivered consecutive 640 × 480 UYVY frames of 614400 bytes through video(4). The operator saw hand movement in the live EmberBSD preview on the board display.
